themes.title: Far-right leaders rally behind convicted killer as political symbol
themes.blurb: Right-wing parties in Italy and Spain are leveraging the case of Mario Roggero, a jeweler convicted of killing two robbers, to push for expanded self-defense laws and challenge judicial decisions. This theme reflects a broader transnational pattern of politicizing crime and justice to mobilize conservative bases.

countries.name: 🇮🇹 Fratelli d'Italia / Lega
countries.note: Matteo Salvini visited Roggero in prison, advocated for his pardon, and considered his political candidacy, framing him as a symbol of self-defense rights.

countries.name: 🇪🇸 Vox
countries.note: Vox defended a mayor accused of causing a wildfire, demanding public apologies and invoking the presumption of innocence, aligning with the broader right-wing narrative of victimizing defendants.

countries.name: 🇺🇸 MAGA / Trump
countries.note: Trump's administration has pushed for expanded self-defense laws and criticized judicial leniency, resonating with the Roggero case's themes.

countries.name: 🇵🇱 Prawo i Sprawiedliwość

countries.name: 🇮🇹 Fratelli d'Italia / Lega
countries.note: Tensions between Meloni and Salvini over policy direction and alliances with far-right figures like Vannacci threaten coalition stability.

countries.name: 🇩🇪 Alternative für Deutschland
countries.note: AfD's NRW branch faces a power struggle between Vincentz and Weidel, with walkouts and legal threats escalating internal conflicts.

themes.title: Right-wing leaders exploit crime and security concerns

countries.name: 🇮🇹 Fratelli d'Italia / Lega
countries.note: Meloni and Salvini are pushing for expanded self-defense laws and stricter immigration policies, citing rising crime rates.

countries.name: 🇪🇸 Vox
countries.note: Vox has accused regional governments of negligence in handling wildfires and immigration, demanding stricter security measures.

countries.name: 🇺🇸 MAGA / Trump
countries.note: Trump's administration has emphasized election security and immigration enforcement, framing them as critical to national safety.
